title_html: By the Time She Reaches the Pilot
title_plain: The Language of Maritime Safety -- SOLAS, Evacuation and the Future of an Operational Plan
menu_desc: Emergency words, reading the two futures of an operational order, and short written answers -- 35 slides
hero_line: An operational order is written in a tense most people never use. That is why it reads as if it had already happened.
grammar_point: future perfect and future continuous in operational planning

vocab.def: the act of moving everybody out of a ship or a space in an organised way
vocab.ex: The evacuation was orderly, and nobody was hurt.

vocab.def: a personal flotation device for each person on board

vocab.def: the fixed system that puts out a fire in a closed space

vocab.def: a section of the hull that can be closed so water cannot enter
vocab.ex: The watertight compartment was closed in four minutes.

vocab.def: the sound or light that tells everybody on board to react
vocab.ex: The company will replace every emergency signal card.

vocab.def: the order to leave the ship at once, given only by the master

vocab.def: a person killed or injured, or the accident itself in formal use

vocab.def: the emergency radio message a ship sends when she needs help

reading_sub: Questions first, then the text. Use the glossary.

paras: This instruction applies to every ship in the fleet from next month. By the time a ship reaches the pilot station, the crew will have completed the safety round. They will have checked the muster list, the life jackets and the life rafts by name, not only by signature. The deck team will be standing by at the bow and the stern thirty minutes before the pilot arrives.

Why this instruction? In February, a fire started in a machinery space. The fixed fire suppression system put it out in four minutes. The watertight compartment was closed, and nobody sent a distress call. There were no casualties.

But the debrief found problems. Two of the twenty-one people on board went to the wrong muster station, because the list was out of date. Four life jackets were in a locker that was painted shut. Luckily, the order to abandon ship was never given.
By the end of the quarter, the company will have replaced every emergency signal card in the fleet. Paper alone does not make a ship safe. Practice does.

grammar_question: Which actions are finished before the deadline? Which one is in progress at that moment? Write the word that shows the deadline.
grammar_rows: finished BEFORE a moment in the future
By the time she arrives, the crew will have completed the round.
in progress AT a moment in the future
The deck team will be standing by at the bow.
by / by the time / by the end of
the deadline. Look for it first
By the end of the quarter, the company will have replaced...
will have completed = finished before. will complete on arrival = at the moment of arrival. A wrong option in the exam often changes one into the other.
grammar_insight: You do not need to write these tenses. Find the deadline first (by...), then ask: finished before it, or in progress at it?

listenings.h: Four Minutes in a Machinery Space
listenings.sub: The chief engineer talks about the February fire. Sound first, no text.
listenings.text: First, I want to say this: the fixed system worked perfectly. Four minutes from detection to control. The compartment was closed, there was no distress call, and nobody was hurt. On paper, it was a good day. But the numbers do not show everything. Two people came to the wrong muster station and asked me where to go. Later, I tried to open the forward locker, and I could not. Somebody had painted it shut at the last dry dock. We were four minutes and a closed door away from a very different day. The order to abandon ship was never given. That is the only reason those two problems did not cost us more.
questions: How long did the fixed system take to control the fire?
Why could he not open the forward locker?
Somebody had painted it shut at the last dry dock.
Why did the two problems not cost more?
Because the order to abandon ship was never given.

pc_desc: The words of a shipboard emergency and the two futures of an operational order. Key words: evacuation, life jacket, life raft, fire suppression, watertight compartment, emergency signal, abandon ship, casualty, salvage, distress call. Structure: future perfect and future continuous (reading only).

paras: By Friday, the second officer will have checked every life raft on board. On Saturday morning she will be working on the new muster list.
By the end of the month, the crew will have done two fire drills. At 0800 tomorrow, the engineers will be testing the fire suppression system.

grammar_tip_title: The Two Futures of an Order (Reading)
grammar_tip_lead: will have + past participle = finished before a moment in the future. will be + -ing = in progress at that moment. Find the deadline first (by, by the time, by the end of). You only need to read them.

media.title: The 3,500-Capacity Cruise Ship Taking on Central America -- Mighty Cruise Ships (full episode)
media.desc: Three and a half thousand people, one muster list and a crew that rehearses the evacuation of a small town. Everything in today's vocabulary exists on screen, at scale.
media.tip: watch the drill sequence twice. The second time, narrate it out loud in the future perfect, as if you were writing the order the day before.

media.title: Abandon Ship Drill using Lifeboats
media.desc: The drill itself, filmed on board: muster, life jackets, boarding and lowering, in the order SOLAS requires it. The words of this lesson are the commands you will hear.
media.tip: pause at the muster and say out loud what would have to be complete BEFORE that moment for the drill to work. That is the future perfect, in its natural habitat.

teacher.s1: Abertura (1 min): Aula no NIVEL NOVO (pedido da professora em 28/09): texto mais curto, frases simples, glossario na tela, 1 listening so e as respostas por ESCRITO. A prova e 100% leitura. Futuro perfeito e futuro continuo hoje sao para LER, nao para produzir.
teacher.s2: Homework check + warm-up (4 min): Ela le UMA frase que escreveu com um verbo da aula 7 e escolhe um chip. Uma frase basta. Anote erro de sentido para o capitulo 5.
teacher.s3: Provocacao (3 min): Ela escolhe A ou B. Espere 5 segundos. Resposta: A (a ronda vem ANTES da chegada). Se ela escolher B, desenhe uma linha do tempo com o dedo e pergunte, com opcoes: is the round finished before or after the arrival?
teacher.s4: Objetivo (1 min): Leia as tres missoes. Diga: today you answer in writing.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: Ten words of an emergency. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (4 min): evacuation, life jacket, life raft, fire suppression. NAO traduza. CCQ com opcoes: Is fire suppression a fire extinguisher or a fixed system? (A fixed system.) Is a life raft a boat with an engine, yes or no? (No: it is inflatable.)
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (4 min): watertight compartment, emergency signal, abandon ship. CCQ com opcoes: Who can give the order to abandon ship: the master or the chief officer? (The master.)
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (4 min): casualty, salvage, distress call. CCQ com opcoes: Is salvage about the people or about the ship? (The ship and the cargo.) Casualty: only dead, or dead or injured? (Dead or injured.)
teacher.s9: Consolidate (3 min): Ela liga os pares sozinha. Ajude so se ela pedir.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: The fire ended well, and the debrief was hard. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Leitura silenciosa. Mostre o GLOSSARIO antes. Avise so isto: o primeiro paragrafo fala de coisas que ainda NAO aconteceram. Se ela travar numa palavra fora do glossario, de um sinonimo simples em ingles.
teacher.s12: Gist (2 min): Ela escolhe a opcao e ESCREVE a linha que prova. Resposta: (b). A (a) contradiz o segundo paragrafo.
teacher.s13: True or False (5 min): Ela responde as cinco e escreve a linha que prova cada uma. A 4 e a mais fina: o texto diz never given.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: The first paragraph is written in two futures. You only need to read them. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (6 min): Peca que ela ESCREVA, para cada exemplo, finished before ou in progress at, e a palavra do prazo (by / by the time / by the end of). So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ com opcoes: if the round is completed on arrival, is the order obeyed, yes or no? (No.)
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela escreve a resposta ANTES de clicar.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (3 min): futuro simples no lugar do futuro perfeito, will have standing, participio sem -ed, e o erro de LEITURA: achar que a ronda comeca na chegada.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Same February, other words. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (3 min): Leia os quatro pares com ela. O segundo (no casualties were sustained) e registro de prova que ja caiu.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (4 min): Ela liga os pares. Ajude so depois de 5 segundos.
teacher.s21: Complete (4 min): Uma lacuna por vez. As oito respostas estao no banco de palavras.
teacher.s22: Quick fire POR ESCRITO (6 min): Ela escreve a resposta de cada uma no chat ou no papel, e so depois voces abrem as dicas. A quinta (troca de AGENTE: fixed system x crew) e o distrator que ela ja viu varias vezes.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: One recording, then you write. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening (5 min): O UNICO listening da aula (pedido da professora). LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar. Primeira vez em 0.75x, segunda em 1x. No fim pergunte, com opcoes: was the fire a good day on paper, yes or no? (Yes.)
teacher.s25: Writing (5 min): Ela escreve tres frases sobre o chefe de maquinas, uma por inicio. Corrija por escrito so o essencial (verbo e palavra tecnica). Depois clique Show a Model Answer.
teacher.s26: Escrita guiada (5 min): Quatro frases com os inicios. Conte quantos futuros com prazo ela usa certo, sem exigir.
teacher.s27: Escrita semi-livre (5 min): Duas frases: o resultado bom e a preparacao ruim. Use o banco de palavras. Se ela travar, de a primeira palavra.
teacher.s28: Producao (4 min): Ela ESCREVE tres frases de uma nova instrucao, cada uma com by, e depois LE em voz alta. Esse e o unico momento de fala da fase: curto e com roteiro.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases do texto. Toque e peca repeticao, uma vez cada. Mostre a reducao natural: will have completed sai como /wIl@v/ na fala.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks fecham a aula e acendem o stamp.
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 8 complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) escrever cinco frases de uma ordem de chegada em porto, cada uma com um prazo (by...); (2) ler um resumo curto de acidente maritimo em ingles e sublinhar todo equipamento de emergencia. Proxima aula: Precision Reading.
teacher.s25b: Writing: antes do pratico (5 min): Tres frases com os inicios: duas com will have + participio e uma com will be + -ing. Aqui ela produz, mas com o molde na tela. Depois clique Show a Model Answer e compare.
